description:
Overview

The Department of Computer Science (DIKU) at the University of Copenhagen invites applications for one or two fully funded PhD fellowships in Human-Computer Interaction as part of the Villum Investigator project TRACTION (Theoretical Research in Human-computer Interaction), awarded to Professor Kasper Hornbæk. The project aims to understand and advance the use of theory in the design and evaluation of interactive systems.

The position is salaried under the Danish AC collective agreement and there is no tuition. The intended start date is 1 April 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter, with interviews expected in late January 2027.

Project and Research Focus

TRACTION studies how theories can help explain when and why computer systems are useful and usable, moving HCI from a craft of methods towards a science of theories, cumulation and generalisation. The centre is a six-year Villum Foundation project that began in 2025.

  • Work with high-level theories (e.g. self-determination theory, activity theory, theory of planned behaviour) or more specific models and frameworks.
  • Empirically explore the use of theory in HCI, including how existing theories are difficult to apply.
  • Use LLMs, NLP or similar technologies to study or develop theory.
  • Develop systems in AI, XR or social media informed by theory.

Funding and Study Structures

Employment and payment terms
ItemDetails
Regular PhD (5+3 scheme)For candidates with a degree equivalent to a relevant Danish master’s (180 ECTS BSc + 120 ECTS MSc). Full-time employment for up to three years under the Danish AC agreement.
Integrated MSc+PhD (3+5 scheme)For candidates with a Danish-bachelor’s-equivalent degree who are or will be enrolled in a DIKU MSc in Computer Science. Up to five years.
3+5 grant portionA PhD grant portion is currently (2026) DKK 7,426 before tax, paid partly as 48 state education grant portions (SU-klip) plus salary for 150 working hours per year of teaching/supervision until the MSc is obtained.
After the MScTwo years on a salaried PhD fellowship under the AC agreement.
TuitionNo tuition for the PhD programme.

Eligibility

  • A degree equivalent to a relevant Danish master’s in CS or a related field for the 5+3 route; or a bachelor’s-equivalent degree plus enrolment in a DIKU MSc in Computer Science for the 3+5 route.
  • Documented research capability (thesis, publication or project portfolio), strong supervisor recommendations and intellectual humility.
  • Background in computer science, psychology, design research or another HCI-related discipline; interest in theory is essential.
  • Fluent English; the application and all attachments must be in English. No specific IELTS/TOEFL score is stated in the posting — check the official page and university rules.

Application Requirements

  • A motivated letter of application (maximum one page).
  • An outline of your interest in theory, previous work with theory and ideas for using theory based on the call (maximum two pages).
  • CV including education, experience, language skills and other relevant skills.
  • Original BSc or MSc diplomas and transcripts in the original language, with an authorised English translation if needed; a certified recent transcript or supervisor statement is accepted if not yet completed.
  • Publication list and up to three reference letters or contact details for referees.
